x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Indeed,
h
the believers have succeeded

is that those who believed in God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and acknowledged what he brought to them from God, and acted according to what he called them to, which is mentioned in these verses, have attained eternity in the gardens of their Lord, and have achieved what they sought from Him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
The believers have succeeded

, he said: Ka’b said: God created only three things with His hand: He created Adam with His hand, He wrote the Torah with His hand, and He planted the Garden of Eden with His hand. Then He said to it, Speak, and it said,
h
The believers have succeeded
, because of the honor it contained.

c: Sahl bin Musa Al-Razi told us: Yahya bin Al-Durais told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Qais, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: When God Almighty planted Paradise, He looked at it and said:
h
The believers have succeeded
. He said: Hafs bin Omar, Abu Khalda, narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said: When God created Paradise, He said:
h
The believers have succeeded
, so God revealed the Qur’an with it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jubayr told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Maysarah, who said:
m: God did not create anything with His hand except four things: He created Adam with His hand, He wrote the tablets with His hand, He wrote the Torah with His hand, and He planted the people of Eden with His hand. Then He said:
h
The believers have succeeded
. And His statement:
h
Those who are humble in their prayers
means, the Most High, the Majestic, says:
h
Those who are humble in their prayers

when they stand in them, and their humility in them is their submission to God in them through obedience to Him, and their doing in them what He has commanded them to do in them. And it was said: It was revealed because the people used to raise their eyes to the sky in them before it was revealed, so they were forbidden from doing that by this verse. The novel mentioned that:

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us:
m: I heard Khalid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he would look at the sky, and this verse was revealed: ‘
h
Those who are humble in their prayers
. ’ He said: Then he turned his face towards where he prostrated.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Harun ibn al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of al-Hajjaj al-Sawaaf, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said:
m: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would raise their eyes to the sky during prayer, until the verse was revealed: “Indeed,
h
the believers have succeeded
. Those who are humble in their prayer.” Then they said after that with their heads like this.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us,
m: “On the authority of Muhammad, he said: I was informed that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he would raise his eyes to the sky, and a verse was revealed. If it was not ‘
h
those who are humble in their prayers

’, then I do not know which verse it is. He said: So he lowered his head.” He said: Muhammad said: And they used to say: His eyes should not go beyond his prayer place, but if he had regained his sight, then he should close it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad,
m: something similar.

x: The people of interpretation differed about what he meant by humility in this place.
Some of them said: He meant by it: stillness of the limbs in prayer.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Those who are humble in their prayers
, he said: stillness in it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: h
Those who are humble in their prayers
. He said: A person’s stillness in his prayer.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Sufyan al-Shaibani, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: He was asked about his statement:
h
Those who are humble in their prayers
. He said: Do not turn around in your prayer.

c: Abdul Jabbar bin Yahya Al-Ramli told us:
m: Damrah bin Rabi’ah said, on the authority of Abu Shawdhab, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement:
h
Those who are humble in their prayers
, he said: Their humility was in their hearts, so they lowered their gaze and lowered their wings.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement, humbled, he said: Humility is in the heart, and he said: tranquil. He said: Al-Hasan told us, he said:

c: Khalid bin Abdullah told me, on the authority of Al-Masoudi, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of a man from his people, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: Humility is in the heart, and that you are gentle with a Muslim man, and do not turn away. He said: Al-Husayn told us, he said:

c: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said, regarding His statement:
h
Those who are humble in their prayers

, he said: Humility in prayer. My father, other than Ata’, said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up for prayer, he would look to his right, his left, and his face, until the following verse was revealed: ‘Indeed,
h
the believers have succeeded
h
Those who are humble in their prayers
.’ After that, he was never seen looking except at the ground.”

x: Others said: He meant fear in this place.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
Those who are humble in their prayers
. He said: Fearful.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Those who are humble in their prayers
, Al-Hasan said: Fearful. Qatada said: Humility is in the heart.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who are humble in their prayers

, he said: fearful and calm. We have previously explained in our book that humility is submission and submission, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Since that is the case, and God Almighty did not mention it, it indicates that He intended by that a meaning without a meaning in reason or goodness, it was known that the meaning He intended by that is generality. Since that is the case, then the interpretation of the speech is what I described before, that: And those who are in their prayers humble themselves before God by continuing what He has obligated them to do of His obligation and worship, and if the servant humbles himself before God in it, the humility of his submission is seen in the stillness of his limbs, and his preoccupation with His obligation, and his leaving what He has been commanded to leave in it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Those who are humble in their prayers.
And His statement:
h
And those who turn away from ill speech
God Almighty says: And those who turn away from falsehood and what God hates among His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And those who turn away from ill speech
, meaning falsehood.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: We turn away from idle talk. He said: From sins.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And those who turn away from ill speech
, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those of his companions who believed in him, followed him, and believed in him, were turning away from ill speech.

x: God the Most High says: And those who pay the zakat of their wealth which God has imposed upon them, and the action with which they are described is their paying it. And His statement,
h
And those who guard their private parts
* Except from their wives means:
h
And those who guard their private parts

, and what is meant by private parts in this place is the private parts of men, and that is their acceptance, guarded: they guard them from doing anything with them, Except from their wives means: Except from their wives whom God has made lawful for men through marriage, Or those whom their right hands possess means: their female slaves. And the ma in His statement, Or those whom their right hands possess is in the accusative case, in apposition to the wives, For they will not be blamed means: For whoever does not guard his private parts from his wife and the owner of his right hand, and guards it from other people, then he is not to be rebuked for that, nor is he to be blamed, nor is he committing a sin for which he will be blamed.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And those who guard their private parts

, except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed. He said: God is pleased with them for coming to their wives and those their right hands possess. And His statement:
h
But whoever seeks beyond that
means: whoever seeks for his private parts a spouse other than his wife and what his right hand possesses,
h
then those are the transgressors

means: they are the transgressors of God’s limits, exceeding what God has made lawful for them, to what He has forbidden them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God forbade them with a severe prohibition, saying:
h
But whoever seeks beyond that
h
then those are the transgressors
, so he called the adulterer among the transgressors.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Then those are the transgressors
, he said: Those who transgress from what is permissible to what is forbidden.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman,
m: regarding his statement,
h
But whoever seeks beyond that
h
then those are the transgressors
, he said: Whoever commits adultery is a transgressor.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And those who guard their private parts.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.

God Almighty says: And those who are to their trusts which they were entrusted with and their covenants, which are the contracts they made with people, careful meaning: they are guardians who do not waste anything, but they fulfill all of that. The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions, except Ibn Kathir, read it as and those who are responsible for their trusts in the plural form. Ibn Kathir read it as for their trusts in the singular form. The correct reading of this in our view is: for their trusts, due to the consensus of the jurists among the reciters on this.

x: And his saying:
h
Those who are constant in their prayers

means: And those who are constant in their prayer times, so they do not waste them, nor are they distracted from them until they miss them, but rather they observe them until they perform them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq:
m: And
h
those who are constant in their prayers
, he said: their times.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq:
m: And
h
those who are constant in their prayers
at their appointed times.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Barqi told us: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Yahya ibn Ayoub told us: Ibn Zahr told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim ibn Subayh, who said:
m: And
h
those who are constant in their prayers
He said: Performing the prayer at its proper time.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They are constant in their prayers.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: They maintain their prayers. He said: Constantly. He said: He meant the obligatory prayers.

x: And His statement:
h
Those are the inheritors
. God Almighty says: Those who have this description in this world are the inheritors on the Day of Resurrection of the dwellings of the people of Hell in Paradise.

In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of interpretation interpreted it: The novel mentioned that:

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is not one of you but has two homes: a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. If he dies and enters Hell, the people of Paradise will inherit his home.” That is what He said:
h
Those are the inheritors

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those are the inheritors
, he said: They inherit their dwellings and the dwellings of their brothers, which were prepared for them if they had obeyed God.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah:
m: h
Those are the inheritors
. He said: They will inherit their dwellings and the dwellings of their brothers who had been prepared for them if they had obeyed God.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jarbaj, he said:
m: The inheritors are Paradise, which you have inherited, and Paradise, which we inherit from Our servants, they are the same. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: The one who is from the people of Paradise inherits his family and the family of others, and the home of the people of the Fire, they inherit the people of the Fire, so they have two homes in Paradise and two families, and that is a home in Paradise and a home in the Fire. As for the believer, he builds his home in Paradise and demolishes his home in the Fire. As for the disbeliever, he demolishes his home in Paradise and builds his home in the Fire. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said something similar.

x: God Almighty says: Those who inherit the garden of generosity, which is Paradise. According to the Arabs, and Mujahid used to say: It is in Roman.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who inherit Paradise

, he said: Paradise is a garden in Roman. He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Eden is a garden in Paradise, in which He created it with His own hand. It opens every dawn and He looks into it, then He says: The believers have succeeded. He said: It is also that garden, Paradise. Mujahid said: God planted it with His own hand, and when it reached it, He said: The believers have succeeded. Then He ordered it to be closed, so that no creation or close angel would look into it. Then it is opened every dawn and He looks into it and He says: The believers have succeeded. Then it is closed until the same time.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Haritha ibn Suraqa was killed on the day of Badr, and his mother said: O Messenger of God, if my son is among the people of Paradise, I will not cry over him, but if he is among the people of Hell, I will cry excessively. He said: O mother of Haritha, they are two sides of Paradise, and your son has attained the highest paradise.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told me, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ka’b, he said:
m: God created the Garden of Paradise with His own hand, planted it with His own hand, then said: Speak, it said: The believers have succeeded. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

c: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Hisam bin Musak, on the authority of Qatada also,
m: the same, except that he said: Speak. She said: Blessed are the righteous. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

c: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Dawud Nafi’, he said:
m: When God created her, He said to her: Adorn yourself, so she adorned herself, then He said to her: Speak, so she said: Blessed is he with whom I am pleased. His saying:
h
They will abide therein eternally means they will remain therein
. He says: These are the ones who will inherit Paradise, they will abide therein eternally, meaning they will remain therein forever, they will not move from it.

x: God Almighty says: And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. We extracted him from it, so the extract is what is extracted from every soil, and therefore Adam was created from soil taken from the surface of the earth. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with their differences regarding the meaning of human in this place.
Some of them said: He meant Adam by it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: From clay. He said: Adam was extracted from clay.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: from a lineage of clay, he said: Adam was extracted from clay, and his descendants were created from despised water.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We created the son of Adam, who is the human being mentioned in this place, from a lineage, which is the sperm extracted from the back of the stallion from clay, and he is Adam who was created from clay.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: From a lineage of clay, he said: The cream of the water.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God’s statement from a lineage from the semen of Adam.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. The more correct of the two opinions on this is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: We created the son of Adam from the lineage of Adam, which is the quality of his water, and Adam is the clay, because he was created from it. We said that this is the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse, because His statement, Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging place, indicates that this is the case, because it is known that he did not become in a firm lodging place until after he was created in the loins of the stallion, and after his transformation from his loins he became in a firm lodging place. The Arabs call a man’s offspring and sperm-drop his descendant and lineage, because they are drawn from him, and from lineage is the saying of some of them: I carried him, the fur of the skin, Ghadhanfar, the lineage of Faraj, who was not immune And the other said: Were you anything but an Arabian mare, a purebred stallion, ridden by a mule? So whoever is: a lineage, the plural of which is lines, and perhaps they are plural of descendants, but not by much, because descendants are the plural of descendant, and from this is the saying of some of them: If foals are produced from it, they will be similar in terms of leadership, except for their noses. And the rajaz poet said: They throw their offspring into her lap

x: He, the Most High, means by His statement:
h
Then We made him a sperm-drop in a firm lodging

. Then We made the human being whom We made from a lineage of clay, a sperm-drop in a firm lodging, which is where the sperm of the man settled in from the womb of the woman. He described him as being firm because he was made firm for that and prepared to settle in it until he reached his task for which He made it a lodging. And His statement:
h
Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot

. He says: Then We made the sperm-drop which We placed in a firm lodging into a clot, which is a piece of blood. Then We made the clot into a lump of flesh. He says: So We made that blood into a lump of flesh, which is a piece of flesh. And His statement: Then We made the lump of flesh into bones. He says: So We made that lump of flesh into bones. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq, except for Asim, recited it as So We created the lump of flesh into bones in the plural, while Asim and Abdullah recited it as bone in both letters in the singular.

The reading that we choose in this group is the consensus of the proof from the readers on it. And his statement: Then We clothed the bones with flesh means: We clothed the bones with flesh. It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: Then We created the sperm-drop into bone and nerve, then We clothed it with flesh. And his statement:
h
Then We produced him as another creation

means: Then We produced this human being as another creation. And this ha in We produced him refers back to the human being in His statement: And We certainly created man may be from the mention of the bone, sperm-drop, and lump of flesh. He made all of that as one thing, so it was said: Then We produced that as another creation.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement:
h
Then We produced him as another creation
Some of them said: His production of him as another creation means He breathed the spirit into him, so he then became a human being, and before that he was an image.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: Hisham told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then We produced him as another creation
, he said: He breathed the soul into him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Arta’ah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas:
h
Then We produced him as another creation
. He said: The soul.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We produced him as another creation
, he said: He breathed the soul into him.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Dawud Ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: h
Then We produced him as another creation
. He said: He breathed the soul into him. He said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said:

c: Sufyan told us on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We produced him as another creation
, he said: He breathed the spirit into him, so he is the other creation that was mentioned.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement: Then We produced him as a creation, meaning the soul is breathed into him after creation.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Then We produced him as another creation
, he said: The spirit that He placed in him.

x: Others said: His creation of another creation, His disposal of it in conditions after birth: in childhood, middle age, nutrition, hair growth, age, and similar conditions of living beings in this world.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father,
m: Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his statement: “
h
Then We produced him as another creation
h
So blessed be God

, the best of creators.” He said: He came out of his mother’s womb after he was created, so it was from the beginning of his other creation that he cried out, then it was from his creation that he pointed to his mother’s breast, then it was from his creation that he learned how to spread his legs, until he sat, until he crawled, until he stood on his feet, until he walked, until he became intelligent, so he learned how to drink and eat food, until he reached puberty, until he reached the age of turning over in the lands.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Then We produced him as another creation
. He said: Some of them say: It is the growth of hair, and some of them say: It is the breathing of the soul.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say:
h
Then We produced him as another creation

God Almighty says: Then indeed, you, O people, after We created you as another creation and made you into a well-proportioned human being, will die and return to dust as you were. Then indeed, after your death and return to rotten remains, you will be resurrected from the dust as a new creation, just as We began you the first time. And it was said: Then indeed, after that, you will die because it is report about a state of theirs that occurs that did not exist. Likewise, the Arabs say to someone who has not died: He is dead and will die soon. They do not say to someone who has already died: He is dead. Likewise, he is greedy for what you have, if he is described as greedy. If he is told that he will do something and he has not done it, it is said that he is greedy for what you have tomorrow. And likewise in everything that is similar to what we mentioned.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Then on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected.

God Almighty says: And We have certainly created above you, O people, seven heavens, one above the other. The Arabs call everything above something a path. The seven heavens are called seven paths because some of them are above others, so each heaven is a path. And in a manner similar to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding God’s statement:

And We have certainly created above you seven paths
, he said: The heavens. And His statement:
h
And We were not unaware of creation
means: And We were not unaware of Our creation beneath them in Our creation of the seven heavens above you, but We were their guardians, from them falling upon them and destroying them.

He says: So from My blessings upon you is that I left it flowing for you on the earth.

x: God Almighty says: Then We have brought forth for you, with the water which We sent down from the sky, gardens of palm trees and grapevines, for you in them. God Almighty specified the gardens that He mentioned in this place, so He described them as being of palm trees and grapevines, without describing them as the rest of the fruits of the earth, because these two types of fruits were the fruits of the Hijaz and what was near it, so the palm trees were for the people of Medina, and the grapevines were for the people of Taif, so He mentioned the people with what they knew of God’s blessing upon them, with what He bestowed upon them of its fruits.
God Almighty says: And We have also produced for you a tree that emerges
h
from Mount Sinai
, and a tree erected in apposition to the gardens, and He means by it: the olive tree. And his saying:
h
It emerges from Mount Sinai

means: It emerges from a mountain that produces trees. I have explained the meaning of the word at-Tur previously with its evidence and the differences of opinion, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Sinai with a fatha on the seen, and they all agreed on extending it. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings known in the readings of the regions, with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

m: his statement:
h
And a tree springing out of Mount Sinai
, he said: It is a blessed mountain in the Levant. And others said: Its meaning is: good.

x: Who said that?

m: regarding his statement: Mount Sinai, he said: It is a beautiful mountain.

h
From Mount Sinai
, Mount Sinai in Nabataean, and Sinai in Nabataean, is a good place.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: Mount Sinai, he said: It is Mount Sinai in the Levant, a mountain in Jerusalem. He said: It is extended and is between Egypt and Aila.

If the saying about this was as the one who said that its meaning is a blessed mountain said, or as the one who said that its meaning is good said, then At-Tur would have been definite, and his saying
h
Sinai would have been from its description

, on the basis that Sinai means blessed and good, which is not known in the speech of the Arabs, so that would be made from the description of the mountain. But the saying about this - God willing - is as Ibn Abbas said, that it is a mountain known by this, and that it is the mountain from which Moses, peace be upon him, was called, and it is also blessed, not that the meaning of Sinai is the meaning of blessed. And his saying:

. The reciters differed in their reading of his saying: It grows. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it It grows with the opening of the ta’, meaning: This tree grows with the fruit of oil.

means:

x: God Almighty says: And indeed, for you O people, in livestock is a lesson by which you may consider, and by which you may know the hand of God with you, and His power over whatever He wills, and that He is the One from whom nothing He wills is prevented, and nothing He wills is beyond His power. We give you drink from what is in their bellies of milk that comes out from between excrement and blood. And for you in addition to that, in them meaning in livestock are many benefits such as the camels that one carries, rides on their backs, and drinks their milk. And from them you eat meaning you eat from their meat.
And his saying:
h
And upon them and upon the ships you are carried
, meaning: And upon the livestock and upon the ships you are carried, on these on land, and on these at sea.

God Almighty says: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, calling them to obey Us and to believe in Us alone, and to disavow every deity other than Us. Noah said to them: O my people, worship God. He says: He said to them: “Humble yourself, O my people, before God by obeying Him. “You have no deity other than Him.” He says: You have no deity other than Him whom you are permitted to worship. Will you not then fear? He says: Will you not fear, by worshipping other than Him, that His punishment will befall you.

God the Almighty says: Then a group of the nobles of Noah's people, who denied the Oneness of God and called him a liar, said to their al-Nas 114:Noah, O people, is only a human being like you, he is only a human being like you, and like some of you. He wants to be superior to you means: He wants to have superiority over you, so he is followed and you follow him. And if God had willed, He would have sent down angels means: And if God had willed that we worship nothing but Him, He would have sent down angels, meaning: He would have sent down angels with the call to what Noah is calling you to, to convey his message to you. And His saying:
h
We have not heard of this that Noah is calling us to
, that there is no god for us other than God in the past centuries, which are their forefathers.

He, the Most High, means, informing about what was said by the leaders of the disbelievers among the people of Noah, He is only a man possessed by madness. Noah is only a man possessed by madness. It is also possible for a jinn to be possessed, so the noun and the source agree, and it is from His statement, He is, a metaphor for the name of Noah. And His statement, Then wait for him for a time, means: So remain with him, and wait for him for a time.

until a certain time, and they did not mean by that a known time, rather it is like someone saying: Leave him until a certain day, or until a certain time. And His statement: He said, ‘My Lord, support me because they have denied.’ He says: Noah said, calling upon his Lord, seeking His support against his people, when his and their affairs had become prolonged, and they persisted in their transgression: My Lord, support me against my people because they have denied.

He means by their denial of Me, in what I conveyed to them of Your message, and the call to them to it of Your Oneness. And His statement: So We inspired him, ‘Construct the ark under Our eyes and by Our inspiration.’ He says: So We said to him when We sought support against the disbelievers of his al-Nas 114:Construct the ark, which is the ship. Under Our eyes means: in Our sight and vision. And by Our inspiration means: and by Our teaching you how to make it. So when Our command comes, meaning: when Our judgment comes upon your people, with their punishment and destruction, and the oven overflows. We have previously mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on the description of the oven’s boiling point, and the correct opinion in our view is to say this with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. So enter therein two of each kind. He says: So enter the ship and carry.
The ha’ and the alif in his saying therein are from the mention of the ship. Of each kind two. It is said: I took him into such-and-such and I took him into it.

i: From taking him therein is the saying of the poet:
x: I was your enemy's enemy, I did not turn back, and they took you on a difficult day.

Some of them say: Aslakat with an alif, and from this is what Al-Hudhali said: Even if they lead them in a strait, they will be driven away as stray camels are driven away. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Then take therein two of each kind, meaning to Nuh 71:and your family, meaning his children and their women, except for those against whom the word has already been pronounced, from God that they will perish among those of your people who will perish, so do not take them with you, and they are Yam who was drowned. And what he means by his statement: of them is of your family, and the ha and mim in his statement of them are from the mention of family. And his statement: and do not address Me, meaning: and do not ask Me about those who disbelieve in God that I should save them, for they are to be drowned, meaning: for I have decreed upon them that I will drown them all.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘My Lord, support me because they have denied.’
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “So We inspired him, ‘Construct the ark under Our eyes and with Our inspiration.

Then when Our command comes and the oven overflows, then take into it two of every kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already passed among them. And do not speak to Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.’”
The Almighty means by His saying:
h
So when you and those with you are settled in the ship

: So when you and those with you, from among your family whom you have carried with you, are sitting in it, high above it, say, ‘Praise be to God, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people’ meaning from the polytheists.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him: And when God delivered you and brought you out of the ark, and you descended from it, My Lord, let me descend at a blessed landing place on the earth, and You are the best of those who place His servants in landing places. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
A blessed home
, he said: For Noah when he got off the ship.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as O Lord, place me a blessed place with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the zay, meaning: place me a blessed place. Asim recited it with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the zay, meaning: place me a blessed place or location.

x: And His statement: Indeed in that are signs means that the Most High says: Indeed, in what We did to Noah, O Muhammad, of our destruction of them when they denied Our messengers, rejected Our oneness, and worshipped gods and idols, as a lesson for your people from the polytheists of Quraysh, and as sermons and arguments for us, by which they may prove our way with their likes, so that they may be deterred from their disbelief, and refrain from denying you, fearing that the same punishment that befell them would befall them. And His statement: And indeed, We were to test means that the Most High said: And We were to test them by reminding them of Our signs, to see what they would do before Our punishment descended upon them.

God Almighty says: Then We brought about, after the destruction of the people of Noah, another generation, and We created them. Then We sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, calling to them, Worship God, O people, and obey Him instead of the gods and idols, for worship is only due to Him. You have no god other than Him, meaning: You have no deity worthy of worship other than Him. Do you not then fear? Do you not fear the punishment of God, by worshipping something other than Him, and He is the God besides whom you have no god.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “So We sent among them a Messenger from themselves, saying, ‘Worship God; you have no deity other than Him.
Will you not then fear Him?’”

God Almighty says: And the nobles of the people of the Messenger whom We sent after Noah said, and what is meant by the Messenger in this place is: Salih, and by his al-Nas 114:Thamud. Those who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter means: those who denied the Oneness of God, and denied the meeting of the Hereafter. And His statement:
h
And We provided them with luxury in the life of this world

means: And We blessed them in their life of this world, with what We made abundant for them of livelihood, and We expanded for them of provision, until they became arrogant and rebellious against their Lord, and disbelieved, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet. He showed me the country in luxury And His statement,
h
This is only a human being like you

, means: They said: God sent Salih to us as a messenger from among us, and He singled him out for the message without us, and he is a human being like us, he eats the same food that we eat, and drinks the same drink that we drink, so how did He not send an angel from Himself to deliver His message to us? He said, And drinks from what you drink, meaning: from what you drink, so the word from was omitted from the statement, because the meaning of the statement is: And drinks from your drink, and that is because the Arabs say: I drank from your drink.

God Almighty says, informing about what the leaders of Salih's people said to their al-Nas 114:And if you obey a human being like yourselves, and follow him, and accept what he says and believe him, then you, O people, will surely be losers. He says: They said: Then you will surely be deceived in your share of honor and elevation in this world, by following him.
His statement:
h
Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones

... the verse, God Almighty says: They said to them, “Does Salih promise you that when you die and become dust in your graves, and bones whose flesh has gone and whose bones remain, that you will be brought out of your graves alive, as you were before your death?” And it was repeated twice, and the meaning is: Does He promise you that if you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought out once, because He distinguished between the first you and its predicate with if, and the Arabs do the same with every noun that they place suspicion on and its sisters, then they interrupt with the clause without its predicate, so they repeat its name once, and delete it another time, so you say: I think that if you sit with us, you will be a doer of good, so if you delete the first or second you it is correct, and if you confirm them it is correct, and if you do not interrupt between them with anything it is not permissible, it is a mistake to say: I think that you are sitting, and it was mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: Does He promise you if you die and become dust and bones that you will be brought out.

And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Far, far, he said: Far, far away.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Far, far is that which you are promised, he said: He means the resurrection. The Arabs add the lam with hayat in the noun that accompanies it, and remove it from it, saying: hayat lak hayat, and hayat ma tabtagh hayat, and if you drop the lam, the noun is raised with the meaning of hayat, as if he said: Far is what you should not be, as Jarir said: It is impossible, impossible for Aqeeq and those in it, and it is impossible for us to continue with Aqeeq It is as if it was said: Al-Aqeeq and its people. The lam was inserted with Hayyat in the name because they said: Hayyat is a tool not taken from a verb, so they inserted the lam with it in the name, just as they inserted it with Halam Lak, since it was not taken from a verb.

x: So if they said Aqbal, they would not say Lak, because the verb could be the pronoun of the name. The Arabists differed on how to stop at hayat. Al-Kisa’i seemed to choose to stop at it with a ha because it is in the accusative case, while Al-Farra’ chose to stop at it with a ta. He said: Some Arabs lower the “ta, which indicates that it is not the feminine ha, so it became like darak and nazar. As for the accusative of the ta in them, it is because they are two tools, so they became like five ten.

i: Al-Farra’ used to say: “If it is said that each one is self-sufficient, it is permissible to stop at it, and if it is in the accusative case, it is like the accusative of his saying: “There I sat down,” and it is like the saying of the poet: Maui, perhaps a fierce raid like the sting of a brand He said:
x: So the accusative of hayat is like this ha in rabt, because it entered on a letter, on rab, and on thumma, and they were two tools, so you did not change them to their tools, so they were accusative.

h
It is only our worldly life

, means: There is no life except our worldly life in which we die and live. He says: The living among us die and do not live, and others among us are created and are born alive. And we will not be resurrected, means: They said: And we will not be resurrected after death.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: Concerning His statement, “
h
It is only our worldly life

. We die and live, and we will not be resurrected,” he said: He says that there is no end to it and no resurrection. They disbelieve in resurrection, they say: It is only this life of ours, then we die and do not live. These die, and those live. They say: People are like crops, this one harvests, and that one grows. They say: These die, and others come. And he recited, And those who disbelieved said, ‘Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you, when you are torn apart, that you will indeed be in a new creation?’ Saba’ 34:7. And he recited, “The Hour will not come to us. Say: Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.” Saba’ 34:3.

x: God Almighty says: They said, "O Salih, except a man who has fabricated a lie against God in his saying, 'You have no god other than God,' and in his promise to you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth." And his saying, he is from the mention of the Messenger, and he is Salih, and we are not believers in him, meaning: And we are not believers in what he says, that we have no god other than God, and in what he promises us of resurrection after death.

And His statement, He said, 'My Lord, support me because they have denied me.' He says: Salih said when he despaired of his people's faith in God, and their belief in him with their saying, And we are not believers in him, "My Lord, support me against these people because they have denied me," meaning: because they have denied me in what I called them to of the truth. So he, may God's prayers be upon him, sought help from his Lord from their harm to him, and their denial of him, so God said to him, answering his question to Him, what he asked: In a little while, O Salih, those of your people who denied you will become regretful for their denial of you, and that will be when Our punishment descends upon them, and regret will not benefit them.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘In a little while they will become regretful.’

God Almighty says: So We took revenge on them, so We sent upon them the shriek, and it seized them with the truth, and that is because God punished them because they deserved His punishment, for their disbelief in Him, and their denial of His Messenger, So We made them like scum. He says: So We made them like scum, which is what rises on a flood or the like, as if it is of no benefit at all. So this is only an example, and the meaning is: So We destroyed them, and We made them like something that has no benefit. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So We made them like scum,
h
so away with the wrongdoing people
. He said: They were made like a dead, decaying tree.
Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us.

c: And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Ghatha’ is like the lifeless ashes that can bear the flood.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: h
So We made them scum
. He said: Like lifeless ashes that are carried along the path.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So We made them scum
. He said: It is something worn out.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
So We made them scum
, he said: This is a parable that God used. And His saying,
h
So away with the wrongdoing people
, means: So God distanced the disbelieving people by destroying them, because they disbelieved in their Lord, disobeyed His messengers, and wronged themselves.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Those are Thamud, meaning his statement:
h
So We made them scum
h
so away with the wrongdoing people

x: God the Most High says: Then We brought forth, after the destruction of Thamud, another people. And His statement, No nation can outrun its term, means that the destruction of any nation from those nations that We created after Thamud will not precede the term that We set for its destruction, nor will its destruction be delayed beyond the term that We set for its destruction, and the time that We have appointed for its annihilation, but it will perish when it comes. This is a threat from God to the polytheists of the people of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an announcement from Him to them that His delay in their terms, despite their disbelief in Him and their denial of His Messenger, is so that they may reach the term that He set for them, and so that His vengeance may befall them, as was His way with the nations before them.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it.

God Almighty says, Then We sent to the nations that We created after Thamud Our messengers in succession meaning: one after the other, and some following the other, and it is from muwatara, which is a name for a group like something, so you do not say: So-and-so came to me in succession, just as you do not say: So-and-so came to me in succession, and it is nunated and not nunated, and it has the ya', so whoever does not nun it is 'ala' from 'watara', and whoever says tatara gives the impression that the ya' is original, just as it was said: mu'azz with the ya' and mu'azz, and bihma and bihma and the like, so it was sometimes used and sometimes left out, so whoever made it 'ala' stopped on it, indicated the kasra, and whoever made it an alif of i'rab did not indicate, because the alif of i'rab is not broken, so you do not say: rayta Zayd, in which the kasra is indicated. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Then We sent Our messengers in succession
, meaning: one after the other.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Then We sent Our messengers in succession
. He said: One after the other.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God in succession, he said: following one another.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Then We sent Our messengers in succession
. He said: One after the other.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Then We sent Our messengers in succession
, he said: Some of them followed one another, following one another. The reciters of the regions differed in their recitation of this word.

x: Some of the reciters of Mecca, some of the people of Medina, and some of the people of Basra recited it as tatra with the tanween.

Some of the people of Mecca, some of the people of Medina, and most of the reciters of Kufa recited it as tatra with the ya’ without the letter ya like fa’la. The statement about this is that they are two well-known recitations and two languages known in the speech of the Arabs, with one meaning, so whichever one the reciter recites is correct. However, I still choose the recitation without the tanween, because it is the more eloquent and well-known of the two languages. And His statement,
h
Whenever there came to a nation their messenger

, they denied him, means: Whenever there came to a nation from those nations that We created after Thamud their messenger whom We sent to them, they denied him in what he brought them of the truth from Us. And His statement,
h
Then We made some of them follow others
, means: So We made some of those nations follow others in destruction, so We destroyed some of them after others.
And His statement,
h
And We made them stories

, means: For the people, and an example that is spoken about among the people. And stories in this context is the plural of hadith, because the meaning is what was described, that they made an example for the people to speak about. And it may be permissible for it to be the plural of hadith, and it was only said,
h
And We made them stories
, because they made a story, and an example that is used to represent them in evil, and it is not said in goodness, I made it a story or a story. And His statement,
h
So away with a people who do not believe
, means: So far away from a people who do not believe in God, and do not believe in His Messenger.

evidence.text: The reciters of the regions differed in their recitation of this word.
Some of the reciters of Mecca, some of the people of Medina, and some of the people of Basra recited it as tatra with the tanween.
Some of the people of Mecca, some of the people of Medina, and most of the reciters of Kufa recited it as tatra with the ya’ without the letter ya like fa’la.
However, I still choose the recitation without the tanween, because it is the more eloquent and well-known of the two languages.

x: God Almighty says: Then We sent after the messengers whose description He described before this verse, Moses and his brother Aaron, to Pharaoh and the nobles of his people from the Copts with Our signs, meaning: with Our proofs. But they were arrogant about following them and believing in what he brought them from God.
h
And they were a haughty people
. He says:
h
And they were a haughty people
against the people of their region, and those in their land from the Children of Israel and others, with injustice, subjugating them.
Ibn Yazid used to say about that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, and his statement,
h
And they were a haughty people
, he said: They were haughty towards their messengers and disobeyed their Lord, that is their haughtiness, and he recited, That is the home of the Hereafter (al-Qasas 28:83).

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they were arrogant and were a haughty people.

God Almighty says: Then Pharaoh and his chiefs said, Shall we believe in two men like ourselves? and follow them. And their people from the Children of Israel are our servants. They mean that they are obedient and submissive to them, obeying their commands and submitting to them. The Arabs call everyone who submits to a king his servant. From this, the people of Al-Hirah were called: the servants, because they were people of obedience to the Persian kings. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said Ibn Wahb told us, he said
m: Ibn Zayd said, Pharaoh said, Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves? We go and raise them above us, and we are below them, and today we are above them and they are below us, how can we do that? That was when they came to them with the message, and he recited, And you will have pride on the earth
r
(Yunus 10:78)
. He said: Highness on the earth.

x: And His statement, So they denied them both, and were among those destroyed, means: So Pharaoh and his people denied Moses and Aaron, and were among those whom God destroyed, just as He destroyed the nations before them for denying their messengers.
God Almighty says: And We gave Moses the Torah, so that his people from the Children of Israel might be guided by it, and they might act according to what was in it,
h
And We made the son of Mary and his mother
meaning:
h
And We made the son of Mary and his mother
an argument for Us against those who were among them, and for Our ability to create bodies from without an origin, just as We created the creation of Jesus without a father.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We made the son of Mary and his mother

, he said: She gave birth to him without a father who was his, and for that reason the verse was singular, and Mary and her son were mentioned. And his saying, And We sheltered them on a high place, means: We gathered them and made them reach a high place. It is said: So-and-so sought refuge in such-and-such a place, so he seeks refuge in it: if he goes to it, and on the example of his action, so he shelters him. And his saying, to a high place, means: to a high place on the earth above what is around him. Therefore, it is said of a man who is elevated among his people, and honored, respected, and numerous: he is on a high place among his people. And there are two pronunciations for it: with a damma on the ra’, and with a kasra on it if the noun is meant by it, and if the action from the source is meant by it, it is said, rabba rabwah.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the place that God described with this description, and where He sheltered Mary and her son.
Some of them said: It is Ramla in Palestine.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me: Safwan bin Isa told us: Bishr bin Rafi’ told us:
m: A cousin of Abu Hurairah, whose name is Abu Abdullah, told us: Abu Hurairah said to us: Stick to this sandy area of Palestine, for it is the hill of which God said:
h
And We sheltered them on a high ground having stability and flowing water

c: Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Ibad Abu Utbah Al Khawass told us, he said: Yahya bin Abi Amr Al Shaibani told us, on the authority of Ibn Wala, on the authority of Krayb, he said: I do not know what Marra Al Bahzi told us that
m: he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention that the hill is the sand.
b.via: I do not know what Marra Al Bahzi

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Bishr ibn Nafi’, on the authority of Abu Abdullah,
m: the cousin of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say about the words of God, to a high place with a place of rest and a spring. He said: It is Ramla in Palestine.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Safwan told us: Bishr bin Rafi’ told us:
m: Abu Abdullah, the cousin of Abu Hurairah, told us: Abu Hurairah said to us: Stick to this sandy area in Palestine, for it is the hill about which God said:
h
And We sheltered them on a high ground
having stability and a spring.

x: Others said: It is Damascus.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Al-Walid Al-Qurashi told us: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
And We sheltered them on a high ground having stability and flowing water
. He said: They claimed that it was Damascus.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: It was reported to me on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab
m: that he said Damascus.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saʿid, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab,
m: the same.

c: Yahya bin Othman bin Saleh Al-Sahmi told me: Ibn Bakir told us: Al-Layth bin Saad told us: Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We sheltered them on a high ground having stability and flowing water

, he said: On a high ground of the highlands of Egypt. He said: And the high ground is only in Egypt, and when the water is sent forth, the villages are covered with the high ground. If it were not for the high ground, those villages would have been drowned.

x: Others said: It is Jerusalem.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It is the Holy House. He said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ka’b used to say: Jerusalem is eighteen miles closer to the sky.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ka’b,
m: the same. The first of these sayings to interpret this is: that it is a Surat al-Mu’minun 23:49 And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture that they might be guided. high place with a level surface and apparent water, and this is not the description of sand, because sand does not have any flowing water, and God Almighty described this hill as having a stable and flowing surface.

x: A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And We sheltered them on a high ground
, he said: The high ground is the level ground.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement to a high place he said: level.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And His saying, with a place of rest and a spring, the Most High says: Among the descriptions of the hill to which We sheltered Mary and her son Jesus is that it is a flat, spacious land with pure, flowing water. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: and a spring, he said: The spring is the flowing water, and it is the river about which God said, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you
r
(Maryam 19:24)

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaid God bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, with a place of rest and a spring, he said: The spring is the water.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Mu’in, who said: Water.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed,
m: regarding his statement, with a place of rest and a spring, he said: the level place, and the spring is the apparent water.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and a spring, that it is the apparent water.

x: Others said: By decision he meant the fruits.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A place with a place of rest and a spring means one with fruits, and it is Jerusalem.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

x: This statement which he made about the meaning of that which has a place of settlement, even if he did not mean by his statement that it was only described as having a place of settlement because of the fruits in it, and because of that, its inhabitants settle in it, there is no basis for it that we know of. As for Maʿin, it is a passive participle of ʿanta, so I help him, and he is Maʿin. It may also be possible that it is a passive participle of maʿna yaʿmaʿan, so he is Maʿin from maʿun. From this is the statement of Ubayd ibn al-Abrash: Weak, or a deep well, or a plateau without a flame
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign and sheltered them on a high ground having stability and a spring.

God Almighty says: And We said to Jesus: O messengers, eat from the lawful which God has made good for you, not from the unlawful, and do righteousness. You say in the speech to one man: O people, refrain from harming us, and as He said:
Those to whom the people said
and he is one man. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la ibn Wasil told me: Ubayd ibn Ishaq al-Dhabi al-Attar told me, on the authority of Hafs ibn Umar al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i, on the authority of Amr ibn Shurahbil:
m: O messengers, eat from the good foods and do righteousness. He said: Jesus, son of Mary, used to eat from his mother’s spinning. His statement, Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do, means: I am the One with knowledge of your deeds, nothing of them is hidden from Me, and I will reward you for all of them, and give you your wages and recompense for them, so do good deeds and strive hard.

x: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And indeed, this, your nation, is one nation. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as and with the fat-ha, meaning: Indeed, I know what you do, and that this, your nation, is one nation. According to this interpretation, that is in the accusative case, in apposition to what is in His statement, what you do. It may also be possible that it is in the accusative case if it is read in this way, and the meaning of the statement then would be: And know that this, and its accusative would be with an implied verb. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with the kasra, and indeed, this as a resumption. In my opinion, the kasra in this as a beginning is correct, because the report from God about His saying to Jesus, O messengers, is a subject, so His saying, and indeed, this is rejected by it as an apposition to it, so the meaning of the statement would be: And We said to Jesus, O messengers, eat from the good things, and We said: Indeed, this, your nation, is one nation.
It was said: The nation in this position is religion and faith.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, And indeed, this nation of yours is one nation, he said: The religion and faith. And his saying:
h
And I am your Lord

, so fear Me. He says: And I am your Master, so fear Me. By obeying Me you will be safe from My punishment. And the word ummah wahidah is in the accusative case as a state. It was mentioned from some of them that he read it in the nominative case.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: That is in the nominative case if it is in the nominative case as a predicate, and he makes “ummahtu in the accusative case as a substitute for this. As for the grammarians of Kufa, they reject that except in poetic necessity. They said: It is not said: I passed by this slave of yours, because this is only followed by the definite article and the genera, because this is a reference to a number. So the need in that is to clarify what is meant by what is referred to, which genera is it? They said: And if it is said: This is your nation, one nation, and the nation is absent, and this is present, they said: Then it is not permissible to clarify the present with the absent. They said: That is why it is not permissible: Indeed, this is Zayd standing, because this needs the genera, not the definite article.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And indeed, this, your nation, is one nation.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as and with the fat-ha, meaning: Indeed, I know what you do, and that this, your nation, is one nation.

It may also be possible that it is in the accusative case if it is read in this way, and the meaning of the statement then would be: And know that this, and its accusative would be with an implied verb.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with the kasra, and indeed, this as a resumption.
It was mentioned from some of them that he read it in the nominative case.

x: The readers differed in their reading of His statement Zubra, so the majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq read it as Zubra meaning the plural of Zabur. The interpretation of the statement according to the reading of these people is: So the people whom God commanded from the nation of the Messenger Jesus to unite on one religion, and one creed, their religion which God commanded them to adhere to, dispersed Zubra books, so each group of them believed in a book other than the book that the other group believed in, like the Jews who claimed that they believed in the ruling of the Torah, and they denied the ruling of the Gospel and the Qur'an, and like the Christians who believed in the Gospel according to their claim, and they denied the ruling of the Criterion.
It was mentioned that he interpreted this as well:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Zabra means books.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, between them in groups, he said: God’s books were divided into parts.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And they divided their affair among themselves into groups. Mujahid said: They divided their books into pieces.

x: Others of the people of this reading said: The meaning of the speech is: Their leaders will scatter among them books that they have created, in which they will argue for their slaughter.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they divided their affair among themselves into sects

, each faction rejoicing in what it has, he said: This is what they differed about of religions and books, each one admiring his own opinion, there are no people of whims except that they are admiring their own opinion and whims, and their companion is the one who penetrated that for them. And the majority of the reciters of Ash-Sham read that as
h
and they divided their affair among themselves into sects

, like the pieces of iron, and that cutting is from it, and its singular is zubra, from the statement of God, Bring Me sheets of iron (al-Kahf 18:96). So some of them became Jews, and some of them Christians. The reading we choose in this regard is the reading of those who read it with a damma on the zay and the ba’, due to the consensus of the people of interpretation in interpreting this, that what is meant by it is books. This shows the correctness of what we chose in this regard, because the zabar are the books, and it is said from it: zabarat al-kitab: if you wrote it. The interpretation of the statement: Then those nations whom God commanded to adhere to His religion were divided into books among themselves, as we explained before. His saying,
h
Every party rejoices in what it has
, means: Every group of those nations rejoices in what they have chosen for themselves of religion and books, admiring it, and they do not see that there is any truth other than it.

evidence.text: The readers differed in their reading of His statement Zubra, so the majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq read it as Zubra meaning the plural of Zabur.

The interpretation of the statement according to the reading of these people is: So the people whom God commanded from the nation of the Messenger Jesus to unite on one religion, and one creed, their religion which God commanded them to adhere to, dispersed Zubra books, so each group of them believed in a book other than the book that the other group believed in, like the Jews who claimed that they believed in the ruling of the Torah, and they denied the ruling of the Gospel and the Qur'an, and like the Christians who believed in the Gospel according to their claim, and they denied the ruling of the Criterion.
Others of the people of this reading said: The meaning of the speech is: Their leaders will scatter among them books that they have created, in which they will argue for their slaughter.

And the majority of the reciters of Ash-Sham read that as and they divided their affair among themselves into sects, like the pieces of iron, and that cutting is from it, and its singular is zubra, from the statement of God, Bring Me sheets of iron (al-Kahf 18:96).

The reading we choose in this regard is the reading of those who read it with a damma on the zay and the ba’, due to the consensus of the people of interpretation in interpreting this, that what is meant by it is books.

The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And those who do not associate anything with their Lord.

m: may God be pleased with her, regarding this: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us: Al-Qasim told us: Ali bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Talha bin Omar, on the authority of Abu Khalaf, who said: I entered with Ubaid bin Umair upon Aisha, and Ubaid asked her: Do we recite this word: And those who give what they give? h

because they will be returning to their Lord. It is as if she interpreted it as: And those who do what they do of good deeds while they are fearful of God, like the one who:

And that from His statement, Indeed, to their Lord they will return: is in the accusative case, because the meaning of the statement is and their hearts are fearful because they, so when the word that preceded it was deleted, it was in the accusative case.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Those are the ones who hasten to good deeds, he said: And good deeds are: opposition, fear, faith, and refraining from associating partners with God, so that is the race to these good deeds. And His statement,

, some of them said: Its meaning is: happiness has preceded them from God, so that is their precedence in the good deeds that they do.

, meaning: happiness has preceded them.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And they are the forerunners in it, then those are the good deeds.

Others interpreted it: And they are racing towards it. The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of Ibn Abbas, that happiness had been granted to them by God before they hastened to do good deeds, and because of what had been granted to them, they hastened to do them. I said that this is the more correct of the two interpretations of the speech, because this is the more apparent of its two meanings, and that there is no need for us, if we direct the interpretation of the speech to this, to change the meaning of the lam in his saying and they are for it to a meaning other than its most prevalent meaning.
